home.tableSub: A passport-size photo has no universal standard: each issuing authority sets its own size. Printed photos are measured in mm or inches, while digital files for online forms are measured in pixels and kilobytes. The table below lists print sizes and digital file properties for popular document types.
home.tableColDigital: Digital file for an online form
home.tableNote: The sizes above are published by the issuing authorities or their official partners. Photo specifications change — always check the official page of the office handling your application before submitting.
home.beforeSub: A passport photo resizer only changes one technical parameter. Three more factors decide whether the file meets the required specifications:

beforePoints.d: The photo must be cropped to the document's aspect ratio with the head at the required height, not just scaled down.
Online forms enforce limits — from 10–20 KB for an Indian driving licence to 10 MB for a US passport renewal. Check the form thresholds before uploading.
Rules depend on the submission platform. A US online renewal lets you crop within the form but forbids scans of prints; a UK application crops automatically after upload.

whyChooseUs.lead: Behind every approved document is a photo that meets a strict set of technical, biometric, and legal requirements. To trust an online service to create an official photo, you, as a user, must be 100% sure that your final image will meet all government guidelines and ease the application process. Here are 11 reasons why over 2 million users rely on PhotoGov for their ID photos.

reasons.t: 1. One Service for All Official ID Photos
ps: PhotoGov supports photos for 900+ essential international document types — from passports to national IDs, from visas to boat licenses. Simply choose the country and type, and our system automatically applies the correct biometric and technical settings for that particular photograph.
PhotoGov uses built-in identification and compliance algorithms based on the essential international regulations:

Government requirements at the country level. All ID photos must adhere to the guidelines of the issuing jurisdictions: [[the U.S. Department of State~https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/passports/how-apply/photos.html]], [[Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada~https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/canadian-passports/photos.html]], [[the UK Home Office~https://www.gov.uk/photos-for-passports/photo-requirements]], and other international ministries and consulates.

Global biometric ID photo standards. On the global level, the ID photo specifications are defined by the [[International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Document 9303~https://www.icao.int/publications/doc-series/doc-9303]], which sets biometric standards for passport and visa photographs. [[ISO/IEC 19794-5~https://www.iso.org/standard/50867.html]] — another international standard that specifies how biometric face images should be captured, cropped, and stored to ensure smooth identification both by officers and automated systems.

When you select a document type, PhotoGov automatically applies the relevant authority’s instructions and checks the image against these ICAO and ISO/IEC criteria for head size, eye position, background, and image quality.

PhotoGov works in any browser, on any device, or operating system. This dual approach gives our users peace of mind during a stressful application process.

The PhotoGov team monitors official sources and updates both the templates and the resource pages when new instructions are published. Behind a simple document selector on our platform, there is always the 100% checked, most current version of the official requirements.
